title: KV: tiered pressure shaper and page-reservation protector to reduce fragmentation and spill spikes
author: Avery Malik
description: Context and motivation: production serving has recently seen bursts where KV cache spill threads and page compaction fight with latency-sensitive inference batches. Spikes in spill IO and small free-region fragmentation cause sudden tail-latency regressions and higher egress/storage costs. This PR introduces a coordinated two-pronged approach: (1) a tiered pressure shaper that smooths eviction pressure and throttles spill initiation using a short-term pressure window and hysteresis, and (2) a page-reservation protector that reserves contiguous page runs for hot KV regions to avoid micro-fragmentation during high churn. Design summary: We add a pressure tier controller that tracks three moving aggregates: recent allocation rate, eviction success rate, and spill IO queue length. The controller computes a discrete pressure tier (low/medium/high) and publishes a policy tuple that adjusts: eviction aggressiveness (scoring bias toward LRU segments vs sampling), async spill batching thresholds, and scheduling hints for the allocation/compaction goroutine. The page-reservation protector implements a lightweight buddy-like run reservation for pages backing a KV arena: when a tenant allocates multiple small objects in sequence the allocator attempts to reserve contiguous runs (best-effort) for the next N allocations; if the run cannot be reserved, the protector delays aggressive compaction for that tenant for a short 'reservation grace' period to reduce ping-pong compaction. Implementation notes: changes span cache manager, allocator, scheduler, and observability hooks. Key files modified: services/kv/cache_manager.rs (pressure controller loop, policy publish), runtime/allocator/buddy_reservoir.rs (reservation primitives), runtime/scheduler/pressure_shaper.rs (integration with batching and compaction), rosie/bench/kv_pressure_bench.py (benchmark harness), docs/observability/kv_cache.md (new metrics), tests/kv_eviction_integration_test.go (end-to-end assertions). Backwards compatibility: defaults keep existing behavior (pressure tier=low) unless heuristics detect sustained churn. Configuration knobs: pressure.window_ms, pressure.hysteresis_ms, reservation.max_run_pages, reservation.grace_ms. Checklist: - [x] Design doc attached and reviewed in ENG-1482 - [x] Unit tests for allocator reservation primitives - [x] Integration tests for eviction smoothing - [x] Benchmarks demonstrating reduced spill spikes - [x] Added observability (pressure_tier, reservation_hits/misses, spill_batched_writes) - [x] Feature gated with config flags for quick rollback Commits (high-level): - feat(kv): add pressure controller and tier computation - feat(allocator): implement buddy-reservation primitives and APIs - perf(scheduler): integrate pressure hints into compaction and batch windows - test: add integration and benchmark harness - docs: add metrics and rollout notes Changed files (high-level): - services/kv/cache_manager.rs - runtime/allocator/buddy_reservoir.rs - runtime/scheduler/pressure_shaper.rs - runtime/scheduler/continuous_batching.rs - rosie/bench/kv_pressure_bench.py - tests/kv_eviction_integration_test.go - docs/observability/kv_cache.md - scripts/ci/kv_smoke.sh Testing and results: Benchmarks ran on dedicated m60 cluster with representative workload (mixed short/long sequences, synthetic eviction churn). Observed results vs main (avg of 10 runs): - tail P99 generation latency reduced 18% under churn (from 312ms to 256ms) - spill write spikes (IO bursts > 4x baseline) reduced by 72% peak frequency - overall spill volume reduced 22% due to better batching and reservation success - fragmentation metric (free-run fragmentation scorer) improved ~12% (fewer sub-page free runs) - CPU overhead: +1.9% across serving processes at steady-state (acceptable) Rollout plan: staged rollout via canary on 10% of traffic for 24h, collect metrics pressure_tier, reservation_miss_rate, spill_batched_writes, then expand to 50% then 100%. Fallback: config flag to set pressure.window_ms=0 disables controller and reverts to previous eviction behavior. Observability: added metrics and logs for pressure tier transitions; added tracing spans for reservation attempts. Related work: ENG-1629 (continuous batching integrations), prior PRs on spillbackoff and compaction scheduling. Risks and mitigations: risk of over-reserving pages causing underutilization; mitigated by best-effort reservation and short grace windows plus telemetry to detect reservation starvation. CI: initial run showed two flaky tests (kv_eviction_integration_test.go::TestReservationRace and bench harness timeouts). Flaky tests were hardened by adding deterministic hooks and timeouts; CI green on final run. Merge notes: squash-merged after approvals. This PR is intentionally conservative and feature-flag gated to allow fast rollback in case of regressions.

release_notes: Introduce a tiered pressure shaper and best-effort page-reservation to reduce KV cache fragmentation and spill spikes. Defaults preserve prior behavior; feature is configurable and rolled out gradually.
notes_for_backport: No API changes; if backporting to release branches, include allocator primitives and disable controller by default via config. Coordinate with infra for canary metrics.
